title: The Standard Mark (ISI Mark) and how it is granted
content: BIS states that under Scheme I a licence to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on a product is granted to a manufacturer after assessing the manufacturing and testing capabilities of the manufacturer and confirming that the product conforms to the requirements of the relevant Indian Standard(s) through testing.

title: Certificate of Conformity (CoC)
content: For some compulsory-certification products the Central Government directs use of the Standard Mark under a Certificate of Conformity (CoC) from BIS instead of a full licence. BIS describes the CoC route as Scheme IV of its conformity assessment schemes.

title: Quality Control Orders (QCOs)
content: A Quality Control Order (QCO) is a notification issued by the Central Government that makes conformity to one or more Indian Standards, and use of the BIS Standard Mark under a licence or Certificate of Conformity, mandatory for a specified product. BIS publishes the list of products under compulsory certification together with the governing QCOs and their amendments.
document_name: BIS: Products under Compulsory Certification (Scheme I)

title: Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) for electronics and IT goods
content: The Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) operates under Scheme II of the BIS conformity assessment schemes and applies to notified electronics and IT goods. Manufacturers apply online through the CRS portal (www.crsbis.in), have their product tested by a BIS-recognised laboratory, and on registration may use the BIS Registration Mark (which is different from the ISI Mark). CRS registration does not involve a BIS factory inspection.

title: Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS)
content: The Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS) is the route by which manufacturers located outside India obtain a BIS licence to use the Standard Mark on products exported to India. Applications are made online through the BIS portal (manakonline.in), and the scheme has its own guidelines, product coverage and fee structure.

title: Products under compulsory certification: Scheme I (ISI Mark)
content: BIS publishes a list of products that require the ISI Mark under a licence (Scheme I) before they can be sold in India. The list is organised by product group (for example cement, household electrical goods, gas cylinders and valves, steel and iron products, automobile tyres and tubes, feeding bottles, clinical thermometers, and certain chemicals) and each entry names the applicable Indian Standard and the governing Quality Control Order.
document_name: BIS: Products under Compulsory Certification (Scheme I)

title: Products under compulsory registration: Scheme II (CRS)
content: BIS publishes a list of electronics and IT goods that require BIS registration under the Compulsory Registration Scheme (Scheme II) before they can be sold in India. Many categories (for example laptops, mobile phones, televisions, power banks and set-top boxes) are covered by the safety standard IS/IEC 62368 (Part 1), while lighting, batteries and some appliances are covered by their own Indian Standards.
document_name: BIS: Products under Compulsory Certification (Scheme II)

title: Difference between the ISI Mark and CRS registration
content: BIS operates two distinct routes for products under compulsory certification. The ISI Mark (Scheme I) is granted as a licence and involves assessment of the manufacturer's factory and testing capability. CRS registration (Scheme II) applies to notified electronics and IT goods, is based on product testing by a BIS-recognised laboratory, uses the BIS Registration Mark, and does not involve a BIS factory inspection.

title: Packaged drinking water and mineral water require BIS certification
content: BIS states that packaged drinking water (other than natural mineral water) as per IS 14543:2016, and packaged natural mineral water as per IS 13428:2005, are under compulsory BIS certification under the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restriction on Sales) Regulation, 2011. No person may manufacture or sell these products except under the BIS Certification Mark. Licences are granted under Scheme I, and foreign manufacturers apply through FMCS.
document_name: BIS Blog: Compulsory BIS Certification of Packaged Drinking Water and Packaged Natural Mineral Water

title: Hallmarking of gold and silver is a BIS conformity assessment activity
content: In addition to product certification, BIS runs hallmarking for gold and silver articles. Jewellers register with BIS, and articles are tested and marked at BIS-recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centres. Since 1 July 2021 a hallmark carries the BIS logo, the purity of the article, and a six-digit alphanumeric HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) number.

title: Scheme I: the official BIS guidelines that govern a Standard Mark licence
content: BIS operates product certification for the Standard Mark under Scheme-I of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. On its Product Certification Process page BIS publishes the guideline documents that govern the licence: Guidelines for Grant of Licence, Additional Guidelines for Scheme-I, Guidelines for Dealing With Product Non-Conformity, Guidelines for Dealing With Unsatisfactory Performance (Other Than Product Non-Conformity), Guidelines for Change in Scope of Licence, Guidelines for Renewal of Licence, Guidelines for Retesting of samples, Guidelines for Factory Surveillance, Guidelines for Market Surveillance, and Guidelines for utilisation of Cluster Based Test Facility (CBTF) by MSMEs. This record names the documents BIS publishes; it does not reproduce their contents, and the detailed procedure, documents and timelines are stated only in those guidelines themselves.

title: Scheme IV: the official BIS guidelines that govern a Certificate of Conformity
content: BIS operates the Certificate of Conformity route under Scheme-IV of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. On its Product Certification Process page BIS publishes the guideline documents for this route: Guidelines for grant of certificate of conformity, Guidelines for renewal of certificate of conformity, and Guidelines for surveillance (Stampings/Laminations/Core of Transformers). This record names the documents BIS publishes; the procedure itself is stated only in those guidelines.

title: CRS: legal basis and what registration grants
content: The BIS CRS portal states that the Compulsory Registration Scheme is operated under the Bureau of Indian Standards (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018 (Scheme II of Schedule II), as per the BIS Act 2016. Products are brought under the scheme by Compulsory Registration Orders notified by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers and the Ministry of Textiles. BIS states: "As per the Orders, no person shall manufacture or store for sale, import, sell or distribute goods which do not conform to the Indian standard specified in the order and do not bear the Standard Mark with unique registration number obtained from BIS." BIS grants a licence to manufacturers to use the Standard Mark with a unique R-number through registration based on self-declaration of conformity.
reference: Scheme II of Schedule II, BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018

title: CRS: who can apply for registration
content: The BIS CRS portal states who may apply: "Manufacturer (factory owner) of any product, which comes under the ambit of the Compulsory Registration Order (CRO) notified by Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers and Ministry of Textiles." For applicants located outside India, BIS publishes guidelines for nomination of an Authorized Indian Representative, a nomination format, and a model affidavit cum undertaking to be furnished by the manufacturer.

title: Where BIS publishes product certification fees
content: BIS publishes its fees rather than quoting them case by case. The Product Certification Fee page offers a search facility for the marking fee for an Indian Standard, a download of the marking fee for all products under certification (Scheme-I), and the Notification of Marking Fee for use of the Standard Mark dated 05.08.2021 together with its subsequent amendments. The CRS portal publishes a separate revised fee structure for registration. Amounts are stated only in those BIS documents and are not reproduced here.
reference: Fee search, Scheme-I fee list, and fee notifications

title: The official BIS portals for certification applications
content: BIS takes certification applications online through its own portals. The Product Certification "Apply Online" page links to the BIS Manak Online portal at manakonline.in, which BIS also uses for the Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme and for searching granted licences. Registration under the Compulsory Registration Scheme is applied for through the separate BIS CRS portal at crsbis.in. These are the official application routes; MetrIQ does not submit applications and does not know the status of any application or licence.
